key_insight: Watermark scores can bound the share of edited AI-generated text in a corpus, but without restrictions on edits, the upper bound remains 100%.
engineering_relevance: Corpus auditors can quantify prevalence uncertainty rather than count detector positives, provided editing assumptions and human-score calibration are credible.
method: Derive power envelopes for Gumbel-max and KGW watermarks using retention, entropy and substitution budgets.
Convert envelopes into identified sets and finite-sample prevalence bounds with exact or independently calibrated nulls.
Extend inference to confidence sequences for streaming corpora.
evidence_signal: Evaluations included simulations, OPT-1.3B and Qwen3-1.7B text, and 12,000 fresh human documents scored under three keys; finite-pool resampling bounds covered, with an exact-null interval of about [0.14, 0.38] at a true share of 0.20.
watch_item: Paraphrasing can violate the envelope, and a simulated null error of 0.01 broke exact-null coverage at 100,000 documents; independent calibration preserved coverage but needed substantial reference data for narrow bounds.
paper_title: Prevalence Bounds for Edited Watermarked Text: Power Envelopes and Calibration Sensitivity
